newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Crash turns Sao Paulo street into burning inferno.
newsitem.headline: Crash turns Sao Paulo street into burning inferno.

text.p: The quiet morning routine of a middle class Sao Paulo suburb was transformed into a terrifying inferno on Thursday when a Fokker-100 aircraft fell out of the sky and exploded into a ball of fire.

The 108-seat aircraft spun out of control shortly after taking off from central Sao Paulo Congonhas airport and crashed through the roofs of several homes before slamming into the front of a house. Behind it was a fiery path of death and destruction as fuel leaking from the plane set streets, cars and homes ablaze.
None of the 89 passengers and six crew survived. Officials said at least eight people were killed on the ground.
"The first thing I heard was this deafening sound followed by a huge explosion," said Washington de Abreu y Silva, a carpenter who was working at the back of his store when the plane went down.

"I didn't stop to think what had happened, I just grabbed a fire extinguisher and started helping put out the fire," said Silva, adding it was several minutes before he realised the plane had torn the roof off the building where he works.

Neighbours said their first reaction was to run out into the street screaming. "I didn't know what was happening. I was so frightened, I didn't know where to turn," said housewife Eusa da Silva, who found pieces of the fuselage strewn around her backyard.

The Jabaquara neighbourhood where the TAM airline Fokker went down is below the flight path of planes heading to and from Congonhas, Sao Paulo's busy domestic airport. Many of its residents are employed by airlines or work as ground staff.

Eyewitnesses said they saw the low-flying plane dive sharply to the right and disappear in a cloud of black smoke. Its right wing slammed into a building of three floors and remained stuck there like an axe in a tree stump.
The plane narrowly missed a primary school where more than 200 children had just begun their morning lessons.
One woman, who at the time of the crash was washing her dog in the street, turned her garden hose on the flames in a futile attempt to save her home.

The plane's central fuselage ploughed into the front of a house and immediately burst into flames. Eyewitnesses said the heat was so intense there was no chance anyone could have approached the fire to pull any of the victims out.
Neighbours said by the time the rescue teams arrived and managed to control the fire, all that was left was a tangle of metal, ash, rubble and foam rubber.
"It's a catastrophe. There is only death and destruction in there. Now it's just a question of finding the victims and pulling them out," said a tearful firefighter.
